title: Test Doubles: dummy, stub, spy, mock, fake
summary: Five ways to replace a real collaborator in a test, each with its own name, purpose, and kind of assertion.
signals: unit tests opening real sockets, SMTP clients, or database connections
a mocking framework standing in for every collaborator, even plain data holders
assertions on a mock's recorded call for a value the test never actually uses
a hand-rolled in-memory implementation of a repository interface used only in tests

roles.OrderRepository: port the use case depends on for persistence (get / save)
roles.InMemoryOrderRepository: fake: real behaviour, no external system — copies on both save and get
roles.PaymentGateway: port for an external, side-effecting collaborator; charge answers approved or declined
roles.StubPaymentGateway: stub: a canned charge result, no assertions made on it
roles.MockPaymentGateway: mock: a hand-rolled expectation, behaviour verification
roles.Mailer: port for a fire-and-forget side effect
roles.SpyMailer: spy: records calls for the test to assert afterwards, state verification
roles.AuditLogger: port for the side effect of a declined charge
roles.NullAuditLogger: dummy: satisfies the constructor in happy-path tests, never invoked
roles.SpyAuditLogger: spy: records the declined-charge message once the audit logger becomes a real collaborator

stages.title: Before
stages.idea: CancelOrder constructs its own mailer and payment gateway. Both are real-dependency stand-ins that throw "network unavailable", so the test can only assert that the use case blows up.

stages.title: After
stages.idea: Every collaborator is injected behind a port. The tests plug in a dummy, a stub, a spy, a mock and a fake — one per role — and name each for what it is. The stub's canned decline drives a branch where the order stays uncancelled and the audit logger, otherwise a dummy, becomes a real collaborator.

checks: What's the difference between a stub and a mock, and which kind of assertion — state or behaviour — does each support?
Why does a dummy exist at all if the test never calls it?
When does a fake earn its cost over a mock, and when is that the wrong trade?
Why does replacing every collaborator with a mocking-framework mock couple a test to the collaborator's implementation instead of its contract?
